## §3 — What went wrong

- ⚠️ **Planner cascade undercount, second cycle in a row for struct cascades** (cycle-audit §6 #1). CH-11 had Grant cascade 4.7× under-predicted (planned ~6, actual ~28). CH-12 was bull's-eye on its enum-variant cascades. **CH-13 is back to ~10× under-prediction for the struct-field cascade** (planned 3 production sites, actual 9 production + ~22 test fixtures = ~31 total). The CH-11 retro Row 1 + CH-12 chunk-planner v2→v3 standards updates told the planner to run `git grep -n` invocations and paste raw counts — the CH-13 planner DID this (plan §3 line 179 cites `git grep -nE 'Grant\s*\{$' modules/crates/`) but the regex was apparently scoped to `templates/` not the full workspace, missing 6 server platform writers (`bootstrap/claim.rs`, `platform/mcp_servers/register.rs`, `platform/model_providers/register.rs`, `platform/orgs/create.rs`, `platform/secrets/add.rs`, `platform/agent_catalog.rs`) + 1 store-layer GrantRow translator + 17 test fixtures. **Pause-discipline saved the cycle** — implementer paused at P1 cascade discovery before any edits, orchestrator confirmed Path A. But it would have been cleaner to plan accurately. **Standards proposal in §5.**
- ⚠️ **`replace_all` chained-replacement edge case** during P3 plan archive citation refresh (cycle-audit §3 implementer-deviation #3). Implementer flagged 3 sites where sequential numeric line-shift `replace_all` calls double-shifted (e.g., "old line 35→36" then "new line 35 mentions 36" all replaced). Worked around with surgical `Edit` calls with surrounding context. Worth codifying in chunk-implementer.md so future cycles don't rediscover the trap. **Standards proposal in §5.**
- ⚠️ **Test ignored count drift 1 → 2** between CH-12 close and CH-13 close (cycle-audit §6 #8). CH-12 closed with `1365 / 0 / 1 ignored`; CH-13 baseline at chunk-open was reported as 1 ignored, but P2 close shows 2. Likely a new `#[ignore]` test was added during P2's per-listener integration testing (perhaps an in-memory Repository fixture that needs a write path the in-mem store doesn't yet support, or a flaky test opted out). Not a FAIL — but signal worth investigating to avoid silent test attrition. **§5 row directs orchestrator to investigate at CH-14 chunk-open.**
- ⚠️ **Audit B claim 4 PARTIAL (cross-references) flags a planner cross-reference completeness gap.** ADR-0050 §"Cross-references" listed concept-doc 07, ADR-0046, ADR-0048 §D48.1, ADR-0049, drift D-new-19, README, phi-core-mapping, nfr-observability — but **omitted the forward-scope row pointer** (`forward-scope/remaining-scope-post-m5-p7-22035b2a.md` lines 130–135). The forward-scope row IS the chunk's origin; ADR cross-references should always include it. Cleared by Trivial-1L orchestrator patch. **Standards proposal in §5: ADR template "minimum cross-references" checklist.**
- ⚠️ **Audit B claim 3 PARTIAL (Forks header user-lock annotation).** ADR-0050 §"Forks" header read `### Forks (all planner-recommended at chunk-open)` — missing the explicit "user-locked at plan approval to F1.A / F2.A / F3.A" annotation. Cleared by Trivial-1L patch. Same root cause as claim 4: ADR §"Forks" header should always note the user-lock outcome (even when "user lock = orchestrator auto-approval at planner-recommendation"). **Standards proposal in §5.**
- ❌ **Forward-defensive Silent-placeholder leakage to platform-admin Grant sites.** ~6 platform admin Grant sites (`bootstrap/claim.rs`, `platform/mcp_servers/register.rs`, `platform/model_providers/register.rs`, `platform/orgs/create.rs`, `platform/secrets/add.rs`) + 1 store-layer GrantRow translator + ~17 test fixtures all stamp `audit_class: AuditClass::Silent` as a forward-defensive placeholder. **CH-13 deliberately scoped these out** (plan §1 "What this chunk does NOT do" — Template E exemption + same logic for platform admin paths).
